quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: How should you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between your vehicle and others gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: How do you know you are stopped at a safe distance behind another vehicle?

options.text: You can read its license plate.
You can see the ground under the vehicle's rear wheels.
You can read its bumper stickers.
You can count the passengers in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the ground under the vehicle's rear wheels.
questions.explanation: When stopped behind another vehicle, stay back far enough to see the ground under its rear wheels. This gives you room to move around the vehicle if needed and protects you if the vehicle rolls backward.

questions.question: When may you honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: What must you do if a train is approaching and could be a danger?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross. This is true even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light before proceeding in any direction.
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Do not park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means the action shown (in this case, a right turn) is not allowed.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
The roadway becomes more slippery as you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, faster speeds make your tires less effective at removing water. If you go too fast, your tires will lose grip and you will hydroplane (slide on water).

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Quickly pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much space as you can. Bicycles have less protection than cars, so do not crowd them. Passing too quickly can cause the bicyclist to lose control.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
The road curves ahead.
Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane on a multilane road will end. Traffic in the right lane must merge to the left.

questions.question: A solid red arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red circular traffic light. Drivers in that lane must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in a business district if no sign is posted?

options.text: 70 mph
55 mph
40 mph
30 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a business district is 30 miles per hour. If a different speed limit is posted, follow that sign instead.

questions.question: What should you do when preparing to turn left?

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down. Move into the left lane before you reach the intersection. Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street?

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle is fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely when you can clearly see ahead, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you, and your vehicle has enough speed to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: After an accident where someone is injured, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Never move the injured person.
Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can make injuries worse. Keep them warm and help stop any severe bleeding with direct pressure until help arrives.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They tell drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: What should you do when a driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Speed up.
Drive at the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass easily.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass easily.
questions.explanation: Slow down when someone wants to pass you. This creates room in front of your vehicle. They can complete the pass faster and more safely.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is present.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You may no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer have to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. But you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
The divided highway is ending.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The divided highway is ending.
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the divided highway is about to end.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.
No, under no circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road or sidewalk. This applies to all passengers and to all parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop immediately and back up.
Difficult driving conditions are present.
You should drive faster to exit the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Difficult driving conditions are present.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is being done on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on the left, and a bicycle is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Try to fit between both.
Let the car pass, then pass the bicycle.
Pass the bicycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: When facing multiple hazards, handle them one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicycle. Never try to pass the bicycle while the car is approaching.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for nearby police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When you turn, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid the red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, go ahead. If you are not, stop.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. Children may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and then:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgaters.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again to catch any traffic you may have missed.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop. Stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. Regulation signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means you cannot park here.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area.
The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on the road. These limits are for ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may move in the direction of the arrow if they choose to.
Drivers in that lane must move in the direction of the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must always stop completely before moving in the direction of the arrow.
Drivers in that lane must move in the direction of the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must move in the direction of the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road tells drivers in that lane to move in the direction shown. Drivers must follow traffic signals and signs before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the road surface up to the top. This is worse in hot weather because the heat makes more oil come to the surface.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Very rare.
Extremely dangerous.
Not a real concern.
As safe as driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle to get better grip.
Get off the highways as fast as possible.
Use four-wheel drive on your vehicle.
Slow down and increase your distance from other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: When roads are snowy or icy, slow down and stay farther away from other vehicles. These are the most important ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light.
A flashing red light.
A solid yellow light.
A solid red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead of you. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be careful when approaching from behind. On hills with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent crashes.
Protecting yourself by passing bad drivers on the road.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see danger and take action before an accident happens. It protects you from aggressive, careless, distracted, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.
